page: Microsoft Azure E96-48s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv5 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The configuration includes 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The system features 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 14.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong memory subsystem performance. The server achieves a large-block read-only memory bandwidth of 263.69 GB/sec and a large-block write bandwidth of 128.61 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 230.56 GB/sec, and Passmark database operations score at 23,498.42, indicating robust data-handling capabilities. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, sit in the average tier, alongside standard LLM inference speeds for small and medium models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E96-48s_v5 offers a high density of RAM relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without paying for excess CPU cores. The lack of local storage requires reliance on external premium storage, which represents an architectural tradeoff. This server is highly suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-heavy data processing pipelines.
